clue.text: Big part of car

definitions.meaning: something big or ... is unusually large, as in a ... crop
the bar across the front or back of a car that absorbs knocks

explanation.surface: A remark that a sizeable chunk of a vehicle is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective meaning abundant, as in a bumper harvest, and the protective bar on a vehicle.

clue.text: A lot of girls drink!

definitions.meaning: a group of young women, the collective noun traditionally used for them
informal British word for an alcoholic drink, as in 'a quick one down the pub'

explanation.surface: An exclamation that many young women are drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a gathering of girls, and British slang for an alcoholic drink, especially beer.

clue.text: Sun now, then … season of rain

definitions.meaning: if it is Sunday now, then Monday is coming soon: the day abbreviation plus a word for shortly
the wet season of heavy rains in South Asia

explanation.surface: Weather forecast: sunshine at present, but the rainy season is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads Sun as the abbreviation for Sunday: when it is Sun now, then Mon (Monday) comes soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal wind of South Asia brings the rainy months, so the word names that wet season.

clue.text: Dance? Did I step on your foot?

definitions.meaning: a dance in which partners may be cut in on by another dancer asking politely

definitions.text: Did I step on your foot?
definitions.meaning: the polite apology one would offer after treading on a partner's toes

explanation.surface: A dancer asks someone to dance and then apologises for clumsy footwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an old ballroom dance where a dancer may claim another's partner, and the polite phrase of apology.

clue.text: Brought up changes to delete, outlining state

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form an outline around the state abbreviation
the word delete is changed into a new order of its letters

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone raises the matter of amendments that would remove a state's boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes to' gives ELETED; 'outlining' wraps it round the state. 'Brought up' reads like raised as a child, but means lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought up in the sense of raised or lifted to a higher position.

clue.text: Spectacular manoeuvre requiring a little room, exercise to assist circling round and round

parts.note: the loo is a lavatory, a small room in a house (British informal)
PT stands for physical training, school exercise

indicators.note: the word for assist goes around the two rings, enclosing them

parts.note: to assist someone is to help them
a round thing is shaped like the letter O
a second ring-shaped letter O

explanation.surface: A stunt flyer needs a bit of space, and exercise helps to keep circling round.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British informal for a toilet. 'circling' wraps the helping word around two Os, one for each 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerobatic stunt in which an aircraft flies a complete vertical circle, a showy manoeuvre.

clue.text: European city's queen divorced, her number up?

indicators.note: in a down entry the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne of Cleves, queen of Henry VIII, whose marriage ended in annulment
she was the fourth of his six wives, written as Roman numeral IV

explanation.surface: Gossip about a city where a divorced queen saw her number come up.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne of Cleves was Henry VIII's fourth wife; 'up' turns ANNEIV into the city. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Austria, in central Europe.

clue.text: See 26
Take apart last of coals within faint remnant of them?

indicators.note: that letter sits inside the word for faint

parts.note: faint light is dim

indicators.note: the final letter of the word coals is taken

parts.note: a glowing ember is what remains of burning coals

explanation.surface: A fire-tender pokes the last of the coals into a faint dying glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives S from coals, placed 'within' the word for faint; the question mark flags 'them' pointing back to the coals.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut or pull something apart limb from limb, so take apart fits.

clue.text: European city's east and north clamped?

annotationWithheld.why: European city's east and north clamped? — the parse puts E and N in VICE, so 'clamped' would be both the word for VICE and the containment indicator, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: European city's east and north clamped?

clue.text: Might fish be second rate, sole off?

parts.note: B is a second-class grade, below A
sole means single or one
as in a price with ten percent off, meaning minus or less

explanation.surface: Is a fish inferior if it has had its sole removed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the flatfish but is the adjective meaning single.
explanation.definitionFit: Filleted fish can be described as free of bones, which is what the clue asks it might be.

clue.text: Regular work in construction of line for old European city

parts.note: regular means steady or constant

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new structure, rearranged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Steady labour on building a railway line toward an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction of' rearranges OP and LINE into INOPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Istanbul, capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.

clue.text: A bandleader overcoming very old musicians, their principles undiminished

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first pieces stand on top of what follows

parts.note: the leading letter of the word band
so means very, as in so tired
lutists play the lute, an instrument of earlier centuries

explanation.surface: A band leader gets the better of some antique players who refuse to compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandleader' is the first letter of band, B; 'overcoming' places it above SO LUTISTS in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolutists hold uncompromising positions, never watering down their principles.

clue.text: Starring me impromptu as showman

indicators.note: improvised and unplanned, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer brags about being given a starring role on the spur of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus ringmaster is the master of ceremonies, a kind of showman.

clue.text: Once more lend an ear if abandoning a new, new church

indicators.note: makes new, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the article a is dropped from the letters before them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A plea to listen if one is leaving a new church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops one A from the clue's letters, and 'new' rearranges what remains; 'an ear' reads as listening but is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To refinance is to provide fresh funding or a new loan, lending again.

clue.text: Go for knife

definitions.meaning: an attempt, as in have a go or have a try
to stick a blade into someone

explanation.surface: A command to attack someone with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt (have a go) and a thrust with a blade, as a verb.

clue.text: Cold beer, duff drink for the brain

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: duff is British slang for faulty or useless, so the word is broken up

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Cold beer goes off, so someone has a different drink for the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duff' (British slang: no good) rearranges BEER into EREB.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, so it stands for the brain here.

clue.text: See 21
Little time grabbed by patient before you, one reflects

indicators.note: in the down entry it comes before, that is above, the following piece
the letter is held inside the word for patient

parts.note: a patient is a medical case
T is the abbreviation for time
ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: A patient seizes a moment ahead of you to look in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-eye is a British road stud that reflects headlights. 'grabbed by' sets T inside the patient, and 'before' puts that ahead of the old word for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A road stud with glass reflectors that shine back car headlights, so it reflects.

clue.text: One singing good number on the whole

parts.note: an alto is a singer in a choir
a numb-er, something that numbs: ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A soloist in good voice sings a number overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as something that numbs, the anaesthetic ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means overall or taking everything into account, on the whole.

clue.text: Pop success overcomes singer, one needing a lift

indicators.note: in the down entry one piece stands on top of the other

parts.note: a hit is a successful pop record
Cher is the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A chart hit beats a singer who needs cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcomes' sets HIT above CHER in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitchhiker thumbs rides from passing drivers, needing a lift.

clue.text: Material that's no problem to take up

indicators.note: in a down entry the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: nil means none or nothing
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A fabric that is easy to take up when hemming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take up' reverses NILSUM in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslin is a fine cotton fabric, a material.

clue.text: Looks and brains too unfair? This is fair!

parts.note: unfair means unjust, that is, lacking in justice
a fair ... is a pretty one, so this describes good looks

explanation.surface: A complaint that having both looks and brains is unfair, answered by praise for beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is said of someone attractive who is clever as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone who has intelligence as well as attractive looks.

clue.text: Dagger providing danger if heading towards the bottom

indicators.note: the leading letter moves down to the end of the word in a down entry

parts.note: risk means danger

explanation.surface: A blade is dangerous if one heads downward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading towards the bottom' moves the head letter K of RISK to the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: No point adding point to pointed items

indicators.note: the compass letter is attached to the end of the word
the compass letter is attached to the end of the word

parts.note: needles are sharp, pointed items
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Pointless to put another tip on things already sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adding point to' puts S, a compass point, after NEEDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, there being no point to it.

clue.text: Does one aim to be more cunning?

definitions.meaning: a bowman is someone who aims at targets
comparative of arch, meaning sly or knowing

explanation.surface: A question whether an aim is to be craftier.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman shooting arrows aims; and arch means sly, so its comparative means more cunning.

clue.text: Stable quality yet to come to a head

parts.note: even means yet or still, as in even better
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A steady trait has still to come to a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, seen in place names like Loch Ness and Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenness is steadiness or uniformity, a quality of being stable.

clue.text: Cross reference?

parts.note: on a treasure map a cross is drawn to show where the treasure is buried

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from treasure maps where a drawn cross indicates the hidden location.
